title: A fixed harmonic relation does not predict the known secondary signal of KIC 5520878 in Kepler quarters 11 to 16
abstract: We tested a constant quadratic relation between two known oscillation signals of KIC 5520878. We fitted local Fourier coefficients in Kepler release 25 raw and corrected flux. A relation fitted in quarters 2 to 10 gives relative RMS errors of 0.950 to 0.956 in quarters 11 to 16, with 10-day and 20-day windows. For 20-day windows, 100 stable-relation controls give smaller errors: 0.077 to 0.158 in raw flux and 0.193 to 0.495 in corrected flux. A separate later fit also leaves large errors. This limited test does not support a constant response at the fixed frequencies. It does not exclude time-dependent or multi-mode stellar models. The flux products share exposures, and there is no independent instrument check. No new signal or planet is claimed.
